name: The Hejnowicz Plane
access: Free, on the open public square at all hours
transport: Fredry tram stop, about 3 minutes' walk
verify_notes: One of four London planes on Plac Wolnosci individually designated as pomniki przyrody (natural monuments) by Poznan city council on 16 May 2023, each named after a Poznan-connected botanist or phytosociologist at the request of the Stare Miasto district council (source: poznan.pl official city news, 'Nowe pomniki przyrody', 16.05.2023). This one carries the name of Prof. Alina Hejnowicz. The four were planted at the start of the 20th century (so roughly 100-125 years old as of 2026) and stand 20-23.5m tall; a dendrological survey including acoustic tomography ordered by the city's Klimat i Srodowisko department found them in good to very good health with low breakage risk. No individual circumference is given in either the GDOS register (which carries no girth field at all) or the primary city article; a secondary press round-up quoted a figure for this tree but I could not corroborate it against the primary source, so no girth is published for these four. Register designation date reads 2023-06-09 (legal registration), slightly after the 16 May 2023 council vote reported in the press, which is the normal gap between a council decision and its formal registration.

name: The Abakanowicz Plane

location.address: Dziedziniec Rozany (Rose Courtyard), Centrum Kultury Zamek, ul. Sw. Marcin 80/82, Poznan
location.neighbourhood: Centrum Kultury Zamek grounds, central Poznan

access: Free; the Zamek cultural centre's halls, corridors and courtyards are open daily 9:00-22:00, though the Rose Courtyard's exact availability can depend on the centre's own programming
transport: Zamek tram stop, about 3 minutes' walk
verify_notes: Designated a natural monument by Poznan city council on 16 April 2024, named for Prof. Magdalena Abakanowicz. Source: poznan.pl official city news, 'Nowe pomniki przyrody', 16.04.2024, which gives trunk circumference 411cm and an estimated age of about 190 years, corroborated by the GDOS CRFOP register entry for species and coordinates. Stands in the Rose Courtyard behind the Zamek cultural centre (the former Kaiser's residence), between the castle and the Arsenal building. Girth at last measurement: 411cm.
